sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- web_search: Web research. Prefer {queries:[...]} with 2-4 varied angles; omit provider unless overriding the default.
- source_check: Gather source evidence with passage citations for a claim.
- fetch_content: Use to fetch URL content, direct images, GitHub repos, and videos.
- get_search_content: Use after web_search, source_check, or fetch_content to read stored content; findText finds passages without paging.

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.project_context:
<project_context>
Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/home/fira/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md">
use typescript, bun, vite.

on naming, use snake case, verb noun for actions, predicate for bools, plural for iterables and records

for coding style, prefer functional programming, be modular and cohesive

prefer self explanatory code over commenting

use function statement for named functions

use type, no interface

use modern tech such as es module

# Workflow

skip git, build, or test by default

use edit to find and replace text that only occurs once. use shell when it fails.

read spec/readme before writing specs

# Web app libraries

- Render components with `h(component, props, ...children)`. Do not call component functions directly (e.g. `h(button, { label })`, not `button({ label })`). This lets React invoke components and preserves hook behavior. `h` is from `lib/web/hyperscript.ts` and is installed globally by the web prelude.
- `h(tag, props?, ...children)` also accepts DOM tags. String tags can include classes, e.g. `h('div.panel', props, child)`.
- do not use semantic html tags for containers. use `h('foo')` to represent `h('div.foo')`.
- `use_state`, `use_ref`, `forward(...refs): (value) => assign to all refs`, `use_effect`, and `use_mount` from `lib/web/react.ts` are project hook wrappers. `use_state` returns `[value, set_value]`; calling the setter with no argument toggles a boolean. Effects can return cleanup functions.
- `s(initial_value, options)` from `lib/web/state.ts` declares shared state and returns a hook. Options used in this app include `localstorage` and `url_param`; `init_localstorage_prefix(name)` scopes persisted keys.
- `use_keyboard(key, handler, options)` from `lib/web/use keyboard.ts` registers a shortcut; use `when` for conditional activation.
- `use_sync_theme` and `use_window_active` are hooks from `lib/web/use sync theme.ts` and `lib/web/use window active.ts`.
- The web prelude `lib/web/global.ts` installs React, web helpers, and shared utilities as globals. For an unfamiliar unimported name, check the prelude and its defining module; don't assume it is a React built-in.
- tsconfig path starts from source, not source/web

## Localization

- `import { text } from 'utility/text'; text('search_threads')`
- on `localization/en.yaml`, define `search_threads: Search threads by title`
- only en for now

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: web_search
toolsAdded.description: Search the web for sources or answers. Full results are stored for retrieval with get_search_content by responseId. Prefer 2-4 varied queries.

queries.description: Run concurrently (up to three at a time); vary the angle

model.description: Model ID; needs provider openai, gemini, xai, mistral

provider.description: auto, all, a name, or comma-separated names; omit for the configured default.

workflow.description: Default none; summary-review opens the curator; auto-summary summarizes

proxy.description: Proxy URL; omit by default (env proxy vars ignored); "" forces direct

toolsAdded.name: source_check
toolsAdded.description: Gather cited web passages about a claim for manual review.

fetchContent.description: Fetch top 5 pages for exact passages

provider.description: auto, all, a name, or comma-separated names; omit for the configured default.

proxy.description: Proxy URL; omit by default; "" forces direct

toolsAdded.name: fetch_content
toolsAdded.description: Fetch web pages, PDFs, GitHub repos, images, YouTube and local video, as the mode allows. Full content is stored for retrieval with get_search_content.

forceClone.description: Clone GitHub repos over the size limit

prompt.description: Question for video analysis or answer mode

mode.description: readable (default): extract readable content as markdown; raw: return the exact textual body using direct HTTP only; answer: answer a prompt using only fetched content.

timestamp.description: Video frame time ('1:23:45') or range ('23:41-25:00'); needs ffmpeg

frames.description: Frames over a range, 5s apart from one time, or over the video

auth.description: authFetch profile name, or true for the only one

proxy.description: Proxy URL; omit by default; "" forces direct

toolsAdded.name: get_search_content
toolsAdded.description: Page through or search stored content from web_search, source_check, or fetch_content by responseId.

content.text:
# Storybook

## Goal

Provide a local page for quickly prototyping and visually reviewing reusable web components with their normal styling and interactive states. The initial page is a simple list of eight atom components with working sample interactions and no component browser controls.

## User flow

1. A developer opens `web/storybook/index.html` through the existing Vite development server.
2. The page renders each component in the explicit list below, without a sidebar, picker, or other navigation controls.
3. Each sample displays the component name and enough props/state to demonstrate its ordinary appearance and interaction.
4. Controlled components receive state and a setter from `app()`. User changes update that state and are reflected in the rendered component.
5. Component styles come from `web/design/utilitarian.css`; Storybook-specific CSS arranges samples and supplies only simple defaults for components without existing styles.

## Page and files

Add:

- `web/storybook/index.html`: HTML entry with a root element and module script for `./index.ts`.
- `web/storybook/index.ts`: imports the project's CSS resets and global web prelude, `web/design/utilitarian.css`, and `./storybook.css`; mounts `h(app)` into the root using React's `createRoot`, following `web/index.ts`.
- `web/storybook/app.ts`: exports `app()`. Owns each sample's state and passes a record of named rendered elements to `storybook({ components })` using `h(component, props, ...children)`.
- `web/storybook/storybook.ts`: exports `storybook({ components })`, where `components` is a record from display name to rendered element. Returns a `main.storybook` containing a `div.storybook_components`; for each entry in insertion order, render an `section.storybook_component` with an `h2.storybook_component_name` and a `div.storybook_component_sample` containing the supplied element.
- `web/storybook/storybook.css`: styles the Storybook page, list, labels, and basic atom presentation where no component styling exists. It does not redesign existing component styles.

Do not modify `web/vite.config.ts`. The Storybook source and HTML live under `web/storybook`, and Vite is expected to serve the HTML entry like the existing app entry.

## Initial component set

Implement these eight standalone atom components under `web/component/` and include all eight in the Storybook list:

1. `button.ts` — `button({ children, ...props })`: clickable action using a native button element; accepts native button props and children. Existing component; retain its current `button.button` styling hook.
2. `input.ts` — `input({ value, set_value, ...props })`: controlled single-line text field; forwards remaining input props and calls `set_value` with the changed string. Existing component.
3. `textarea.ts` — `textarea({ value, set_value, ...props })`: controlled multiline text field; forwards remaining textarea props and calls `set_value` with the changed string. Existing component.
4. `checkbox.ts` — `checkbox({ checked, set_checked, ...props })`: controlled boolean checkbox; forwards native checkbox props and reports checked state changes.
5. `switch.ts` — `switch({ checked, set_checked, ...props })`: controlled boolean toggle switch; forwards relevant button props and reports toggled state.
6. `select.ts` — `select({ value, set_value, options, ...props })`: controlled native select; options are `{ value, label }[]`, and changes report the selected value.
7. `radio_group.ts` — `radio_group({ value, set_value, options, ...props })`: controlled single-choice group; options are `{ value, label }[]`, and changes report the selected value.
8. `slider.ts` — `slider({ value, set_value, min?, max?, step?, ...props })`: controlled range input; defaults are `min: 0`, `max: 100`, and `step: 1`; changes report a number.
Use native HTML elements for interactive atoms. Props should pass through to the underlying element except for component-specific props consumed by the component. Use controlled `value`/`checked` plus setter pairs for mutable selection and entry components. The existing `button`, `input`, and `textarea` modules may be updated to meet these signatures while preserving current behavior.

Do not include app-level compositions such as `sidebar`, `conversation`, or modal components.

## Samples and data flow

`app()` owns and initializes sample state as follows:

- `input` and `textarea`: empty string values.
- `checkbox` and `switch`: `false`.
- `select`: first option selected; options `One`, `Two`, and `Three` with corresponding lowercase values.
- `radio_group`: first option selected; options `One`, `Two`, and `Three` with corresponding lowercase values.
- `slider`: value `50`, defaults for min/max/step.
- `button`: label `Button`; no extra behavior required.
Each controlled sample receives its current state and setter. `storybook({ components })` receives already-created React elements, not component functions, so React renders component functions and their hooks normally. It renders entries in record insertion order. The Storybook wrapper does not provide additional controls beyond the component samples themselves.

## Returned markup anatomy

`storybook({ components })` returns this class structure:

```text
main.storybook
└── div.storybook_components
    └── section.storybook_component (one per component)
        ├── h2.storybook_component_name
        └── div.storybook_component_sample
            └── supplied component element
```

The component name heading contains the record key as visible text. The sample wrapper contains the supplied element without additional labels or controls. These class names are the Storybook layout hooks; individual atom classes belong to their component implementations.

## Styling

The Storybook entry imports `web/design/utilitarian.css`, as the main app does. The page uses existing surface, text, typography, spacing, and radius variables. Use a single-column list, page padding `var(--spacing-4)`, consistent list gap `var(--spacing-3)`, and sample section padding `var(--spacing-3)`. Keep the layout fluid at narrow widths; do not add a fixed-width canvas or device frame.

Existing `.button`, `.input`, and `.textarea` styles should be reused. Add minimal styles for the new atoms in `web/design/utilitarian.css` or `web/storybook/storybook.css` as appropriate, using the existing variables; avoid polished or elaborate variants. The switch should visually distinguish checked and unchecked states; checkbox, select, radio group, and slider should remain recognizable native controls.

Do not add keyboard-navigation abstractions, custom keyboard bindings, or an external component library as part of this feature.

## Not in initial scope

No sidebar, search, filtering, prop-editing controls, separate routes per component, code display, app-level compositions, or generalized keyboard-navigation abstraction.
